When wet-bulb heat index exceeds 40°C, direct sunlight exposure causes rapid dehydration and life-threatening heat illness.

• Drink safe water regularly (2.5–3 liters daily minimum), even before feeling thirsty.
• Keep oral rehydration salts (ORS/স্যালাইন) accessible at home and during travel.
• Avoid heavy outdoor manual labor during peak sunlight hours (11:00 AM – 3:30 PM).
• Wear loose, light-colored cotton clothing and wide-brimmed umbrellas or caps.
• Never leave children, elderly, or pets inside closed unventilated spaces.

• Heat Exhaustion: Heavy sweating, pale skin, muscle cramps, dizziness, nausea.\n• Heatstroke (EMERGENCY): Body temperature > 40°C (104°F), hot red dry or clammy skin, confusion, loss of consciousness, rapid pulse.

• Move victim immediately to shaded, well-ventilated area.
• Cool the body: apply wet cloths, pour room-temperature water on head and neck, fan vigorously.
• Place ice packs or cold cloths under armpits and groin.
• If conscious and not vomiting, give cool water or ORS in small sips.
• DIAL 999 or 16263 (Shastho Batayan) IMMEDIATELY if unconscious or unresponsive.
Action steps by disaster type & stage

• Know your local high-ground shelter and elevation route.
• Move cattle and livestock to elevated earthen mounds (Killa).
• Pack waterproof emergency grab bags with dry food, water, torch, and medicines.
• Secure house roof and store grain/seeds above flood level.

• Follow local union disaster management committee warning signals.
• Evacuate early before water currents make paths impassable.
• Never attempt to cross flooded streams or submerged roads on foot or bike.
• Avoid touch with downed power lines or electric poles in water.

• Return home only after local authorities declare water receded safely.\n• Boil drinking water or use water purification tablets (Halazone/WPT) for at least 1 minute.\n• Inspect buildings for structural damage or snake infestations before entering.

• Reinforce house pillars and fasten tin roofs with rope anchors.\n• Monitor BMD cyclone warning signals (Signal 1 to 10).\n• Keep cyclone grab bags ready and identify your nearest multipurpose cyclone shelter.

• Move to designated cyclone shelter when Signal 4 or higher is hoisted.\n• Assist pregnant women, elderly, children, and persons with disabilities first.\n• Stay indoors inside the reinforced shelter; do not venture out during the lull (eye of the storm).
• Beware of loose electric wires, fallen trees, and ruptured gas pipes.\n• Check in with family and community volunteers at shelter.
• Identify safe spots in every room: under sturdy desks, tables, or against interior walls.\n• Fasten tall shelves, gas cylinders, and heavy items securely.
• DROP, COVER, and HOLD ON.\n• If outdoors, move to open grounds away from buildings, utility poles, and glass facades.\n• Do NOT use elevators during or immediately after shocks.
• Check for gas leaks, fires, and structural cracks.\n• Expect aftershocks; evacuate high-rise buildings via stairwells calmly.
• Keep fire extinguisher, water buckets, or sand buckets near kitchen.\n• Never block apartment exit doors or emergency stairs.
• Stay low beneath smoke where air is cleaner; cover nose with wet cloth.\n• Feel door handles before opening; if hot, do not open.\n• Call 999 Fire Service immediately.
• Wait for fire department all-clear before re-entering buildings.

⚠️ WARNING EXPIRED: This bulletin has passed its validity period. Preserved for reference only; do NOT rely on it as current.

• Know your local high-ground shelter and elevation route.
• Move cattle and livestock to elevated earthen mounds (Killa).
• Pack waterproof emergency grab bags with dry food, water, torch, and medicines.
• Secure house roof and store grain/seeds above flood level.

• Disconnect electrical main switch and turn off household gas valves before water enters.\n• Move family members and essential grab-bags to highest interior floor or plinth.\n• Unfasten domestic animals so they are not trapped if water levels rise suddenly.

• Clear mud and flood silt safely wearing boots and gloves.\n• Clean and disinfect tubewell plinth with bleaching powder before resuming use.\n• Inspect buildings for structural foundation damage before full reoccupation.

• Monitor official FFWC bulletins and local Union Parishad loudspeaker alerts closely.\n• Prepare elderly, pregnant women, children, and persons with disabilities for early departure before access roads are submerged.\n• Select verified high-elevation routes to your nearest designated flood shelter.

• Follow official evacuation orders immediately without delay.
• NEVER attempt to walk, swim, drive, or cycle through moving floodwaters (just 15 cm of moving water can knock down an adult).
• Avoid touching downed power lines, transformers, or electric poles standing in floodwater.
• Move exclusively along high embankments or board authorized volunteer rescue boats.

• Return home ONLY after Upazila administration and Union disaster committee declare it safe.\n• Beware of snakes, scorpions, and hazardous debris hiding inside submerged homes.\n• Boil drinking water for at least 1 minute or use Halazone/WPT water purification tablets.

• Clean local home and union drainage gutters before monsoon downpours.\n• Raise doorway plinths with sandbags if situated in low-lying depression areas.\n• Store 3 days of safe drinking water and dry foods on elevated shelves.

• Avoid wading through waterlogged streets; hidden open manholes and drain covers pose fatal hazards.\n• Never touch submerged street lamp posts, transformers, or outdoor electric cables.\n• Stay indoors and disconnect sensitive appliances during severe thunderstorm and lightning activity.

• Disinfect stagnant waterlogged yard areas with bleaching powder once water drains.\n• Empty puddles in open tires and pots to eliminate Aedes mosquito breeding sites.\n• Wash exposed skin thoroughly with soap and safe water.

• Memorize and write down 2 essential family contact numbers on waterproof paper.\n• Nominate an out-of-district relative or focal person as the designated family check-in contact.\n• Agree on a pre-planned high-ground meeting point in case family members are separated during sudden evacuation.

• Keep mobile phones on battery saver mode; avoid gaming, videos, and unnecessary calls.\n• Use SMS text messages instead of voice calls to communicate when cellular networks are congested.\n• Inform your designated family focal person of your destination shelter before departing.
• Send confirmation SMS as soon as you arrive at a safe designated shelter.\n• Register family names with the Union Parishad or Red Crescent shelter volunteer desk.

• Gather national IDs (NID), birth registration certificates, land ownership deeds (দলিল), and bank books.\n• Place all original certificates and vaccination cards inside double-layer waterproof ziplock bags.\n• Store a photocopy and waterproof flash drive backup in your household grab-bag.
• Keep the waterproof document pouch inside your personal backpack or strapped to your upper body above waist height.\n• Never leave critical land and identification records behind in low ground.
• Keep documents sealed until you reach a dry, secure shelter environment.\n• Report any lost identity records to the local Upazila disaster assistance camp.

• Pack a 72-hour survival kit: 3 liters drinking water per person/day, non-perishable dry food (Chira, Muri, Gur).\n• Waterproof LED torch, spare batteries, fully charged power bank, and safety whistle.\n• First aid kit, antiseptic ointment, and a 7-day supply of essential chronic family prescriptions (BP, Insulin, Asthma).
• Carry the emergency kit on your back, leaving both hands free for balance and assisting children.\n• Keep oral rehydration salts (ORS) and water purification tablets within immediate reach.
• Replenish consumed food and water stocks as soon as emergency relief reaches the shelter.\n• Safely store survival gear for subsequent seasonal flood and monsoon cycles.

Educational Guidance Only: General disaster resilience instructions. NOT a substitute for current official emergency instructions, flood bulletins, or evacuation orders from local authorities and FFWC/BMD/CPP.
